newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Clear NZ spends $14 mln on fibre optic networks.
newsitem.headline: Clear NZ spends $14 mln on fibre optic networks.

text.p: Clear Communications said on Tuesday had spent $14 million fleshing out its fibre-optic networks in Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch along with extending its backbone to Whangarei as it gears up for local competition.
The company completed its first loop in and around the lower half of Queen Street in the heart of Auckland's central business district last month, NZPA reported.
Another loop is about to be built to expand penetration in the general central city area, but precise details are unavailable.
Earlier this year Clear Communications local service product manager Linda Harvey said the company would offer local service where there were concentrations of customers interested in the product.

Clear spokesman Ian Parkes says Clear now has access to all buildings in the Auckland central business district from the ring and has been steadily signing up customers who connect directly to the Clear network.
One of those customers is Supplycorp.
In Wellington Clear is about to complete the building of its second ring, he says.
Work on the Christchurch ring continues, although there are no South Island direct customers yet.
